8.without any reason hasna band kr deti h , andhere me roti lgti h jbki sab kuchh achha chal rha hota h

post_text: I’ve read a lot of mindset books, and most of them feel like variations of the same message. So I wasn’t expecting much when someone mentioned Banned Money Secrets by Sefirelu. But what caught my attention was how they described him — not just the content, but the author himself. Apparently, he’s not very public, doesn’t do interviews, and his work has even been removed from some platforms. That alone made me curious. Reading the book felt less like being taught something and more like being reminded of something I already knew but had forgotten. Sefirelu writes with this calm confidence — like he’s not trying to convince you, he’s just laying it out for whoever is ready to hear it. No hype. No preaching. Just perspective. It wasn’t some magical transformation, but after finishing the book, I started noticing the way I talked about money. The way I thought about lack. And I slowly started shifting that. And yeah, things started feeling lighter. More aligned. I don’t know who Sefirelu guys really is, but I get the sense that he knows something most people don’t — and he’s chosen to share just enough of it with the people who are actually paying attention.

post_text:
This scene hit me so hard. Whenever I have to convey anything to my parents I have to shout, scream, cry otherwise they don't just listen, ignore  me so casually and when they listen as no other option left they are so adamant and deny they did nothing wrong, dismiss it and invalidate it just like here Kaira's father did by saying -thodi si emotional hai. All this because things get so overwhelmed for me that I have to vent, because of all the unfair, injustice, abandoned feelings as when I needed them the most they were not there, as in physically there but emotionally not.          For years till today whenever I want to talk with them about something they never hear me, and later from time to time they keep saying why you don't sit with us or talk to us. I have grown up seeing my parents doing bad quarrels, fights, shouting, disrespecting each other, mother has suffered from many unfair things from her in-laws, etc. I have trauma, that I wake up in the middle of the night fearing they are fighting, in the middle of some work in my room when I hear some voice I fear they again started fighting when they aren't.         When they fight they come barging into my room to take sides, and when I try to point to who is wrong and who is not then again get blamed why I chose him or her, I cry cry and cry, request them to not fight because it gets so horrible and painful to me to tolerate it. Then I am called dramatic. Because I am their child and when they say something I have to leave everything and listen to them but the opposite never happens.                 So I don't believe that parents' love for child is unconditional, no. There are million other things which has proved this. I am the elder girl child, I suddenly became the "matured one" when my brother was born but not matured enough to say something important in matters that affect me. 
              So I am shit scared, trauma about marriage and having children. I don't want to suffer from all this and give my children the same even unknowingly what I have gone through, that's unfair to that child.

I’ve been thinking about creating a small, genuine space for people who are dealing with stress, anxiety, overthinking, loneliness, emotional burnout or simply feel mentally exhausted sometimes.

Not therapy.
Not fake motivational talks.
Just a real and interactive support space where people can feel heard, connected and mentally lighter.

The idea includes:

* Daily mood check-ins
* Anonymous sharing
* Small discussions & problem-solving sessions
* Fun activities & mind-engaging tasks
* Late night talks when needed
* Positive routines & emotional support
* Outdoor meetups/walks eventually
* A space where nobody feels alone in their own mind

Right now, I’m looking for the first 20 core members — people who genuinely want to work on themselves, heal gradually, stay mentally engaged and become part of a healthy support system with others going through similar things.

This is not for spectators or inactive members.
Only for people who genuinely want to participate, connect and deal with things together in a better way. ??

If this resonates with you, message me personally 81093-81319

gave my heart without calculating.
I loved without keeping score.
I stayed even when it hurt.
For six long years, I believed in someone who only believed in what I could give.
I supported her dreams,
I sacrificed my peace,
I ignored my own pain—
and when she reached where she wanted to be,
she left me like I was nothing.
Still, I tried again.
I trusted again.
I helped again.
I believed again.
I gave my time, my energy, my money—
even bought a ?56,000 certification so she could build her future.
And when she no longer needed me,
she erased me from her life.
Now I lie here with broken bones
and an even more broken soul.
I cry every day.
I smile for people.
But inside, I feel empty.
I never cheated.
I never betrayed.
I never played with anyone’s heart.
So why did everyone play with mine?
I didn’t want luxury.
I only wanted loyalty.
I didn’t want perfection.
I just wanted to be chosen.
God, I am tired.
Not of living…
but of hurting.

post_text:
To anyone that needs to hear this:
I don't know you, your name, your story, what your childhood was like, or what happened to you this morning that still hurts when you think about it. I don’t know what you are carrying inside, what battles you are fighting in silence, or how many nights you have spent lying awake wishing things were different. But even as a stranger, there is something I need you to know: your life matters. It doesn't matter because of your grades, your job, your appearance, or your talents; it matters because you are a human being, and there has never been another person exactly like you in the entire history of the world.
Maybe you’re tired—exhausted in a way that sleep cannot fix. Maybe you’ve become so used to surviving that you can't remember what it feels like to truly live, and every day feels like a mountain you are struggling to climb. If that is where you are right now, I am so sorry, because nobody deserves to carry that kind of pain alone.
But please remember that the way you feel today is not a prediction of your future. Human beings are constantly changing, and life changes in ways we never expect. There are beautiful things ahead of you that you cannot see from where you are standing right now. There are people you haven't met yet who are going to love you, friendships that haven't started, and moments where you’ll laugh so hard your stomach hurts. There are sunsets you haven't watched, songs you haven't heard, and adventures you haven't taken yet. None of those moments can happen if you aren't here to meet them.
If the future feels too big, don't think about it. Just think about the next hour, or the next breath. Focus on getting through today: drink some water, listen to a song, wrap yourself in a blanket, and watch the sunrise tomorrow. Give yourself permission to exist without having all the answers.
You don't have to be strong all the time. You are allowed to be angry, confused, scared, and overwhelmed; struggling does not mean you are failing. We affect people in ways we will never fully understand, and the fact that you can't see your impact doesn't mean it isn't there. You are irreplaceable. Please keep going long enough to discover the person you are still becoming, because there are more reasons to stay than your pain is allowing you to see. If nothing else, please stay for me.

post_text:
I don’t know who needs to read this, but I hope this reaches the right person.
If you’ve been feeling overwhelmed, stressed, or like everything is too much lately, you are not alone. A lot of people go through things they don’t talk about. Some people feel pressure from school, friends, family, or even from themselves. And sometimes it can all build up until it feels like you’re carrying more than you can explain.
